walkthroughs.body_html:
Kinematics — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Kinematics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Kinematics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s² for 3 seconds. Final velocity is:
options: 12 m/s
7 m/s

mcqs.q: Which SUVAT equation does NOT involve t?
options: v² = u² + 2as
v = u + at
s = ut + ½at²
11 — substitute carefully: 5 - 2(-3) = 5 + 6 = 11.
9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
-1, by computing 5 - 2 x 3 and ignoring the negative.
-11, by computing 5 - 2 x -3 = 3 x -3 = -9, then -11.
-11, by computing 5 - 2 x -3 = 3 x -3 = -9, then -11.
8xy, by combining all terms regardless of variable.
9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
5x + 3y — combine like terms (3x + 2x and 4y - y).

mcqs.q: Can Pythagoras' theorem be used on any triangle?
options: 9xy, by adding all the numbers and merging the letters.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
No — it only applies to right-angled triangles.
Yes — it works on any triangle as long as you square the sides.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Speed vs velocity”?
options: Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
Displacement s (vector); velocity v = ds/dt; acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt². All are vectors in 2D/3D.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Variable acceleration”?
options: Take a = g = 9.8 m/s² downward (or 9.81). Use SUVAT for projectiles, free fall.
Slope = acceleration; area under graph = displacement. Helpful for visualising motion.
If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
For constant acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ((u+v)/2)t. Useful when a is constant.

If a depends on t: v = ∫a dt; s = ∫v dt. Use calculus rather than SUVAT.
Speed is scalar (magnitude of velocity). Velocity is vector — has direction.
